traveler: David ben Jesse, King of Israel
title: The Sling and the Threshing Floor: the Shepherd of Bethlehem, the Fugitive, and the King in Jerusalem
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Bethlehem of Ephrathah, a son born to Jesse
stops.date_confidence: traditional; c. 1040 BC is a conventional reckoning back from the reign lengths in 2 Samuel 5, not a recorded year, and no source outside the Hebrew Bible notes the birth at all
stops.campa: A son is born in Bethlehem of Ephrathah, in the hill country of Judah, to Jesse, four generations down from Boaz and Ruth the Moabitess who gleaned in that same barley. The books do not agree on his rank among the brothers: First Samuel makes him the eighth and youngest, First Chronicles counts the sons of Jesse and stops at seven. The record gives him no other schooling: he grows up keeping his father's sheep in the wadis east of the town, learning the sling and the lyre, killing a lion and a bear at the flock.
suggested_refs: The genealogy of Ruth 4:17-22, which runs Boaz to Obed to Jesse to David
1 Chronicles 2:13-15, where David is the seventh son and not the eighth

stops.name: Bethlehem, Samuel and the horn of oil
stops.date_confidence: traditional; the biblical narrative gives no date and the figure is a modern convention
stops.campa: Samuel comes down from Ramah with a heifer and a horn of oil, saying he has come to sacrifice, because Saul still reigns and would kill him for the truth. Jesse's sons pass before him one by one. Eliab is tall and Samuel is certain, and is told he is wrong. Seven pass and none is chosen. Are here all thy children, the prophet asks, and Jesse says there remaineth yet the youngest, and behold, he keepeth the sheep. They send and fetch him in from the flock, and Samuel pours the oil on his head in the midst of his brothers. No one outside that room is told.
stops.quote: Look not on his countenance, or on the height of his stature; because I have refused him: for the Lord seeth not as man seeth; for man looketh on the outward appearance, but the Lord looketh on the heart.
suggested_refs: The traditional town centre of Bethlehem, near the Church of the Nativity precinct

stops.name: Gibeah of Saul, the lyre in the dark hall
stops.date_confidence: traditional; the two lenses of this file's research disagreed, one placing the arrival at court c. 1025 and the other c. 1020, and c. 1020 is the figure chosen here
stops.campa: The spirit of the Lord departs from Saul and an evil spirit troubles him, and his servants say, find a man who is a cunning player on an harp. They bring the shepherd from Bethlehem with an ass laden with bread and a bottle of wine and a kid. He plays, and the king is refreshed, and Saul loves him greatly and makes him his armour-bearer. The same book will shortly have Saul stare across the Elah valley at this same young man and ask Abner whose son that youth is, as though he had never seen him. Both passages stand.
suggested_refs: Tell el-Ful, the mound generally identified with Gibeah of Saul
The doublet of 1 Samuel 16:21-22 against 1 Samuel 17:55-58

stops.name: The Valley of Elah, the champion of Gath
stops.date_confidence: traditional; the research lenses gave c. 1020 and c. 1025-1020 for the same duel, and c. 1020 is used here
stops.campa: Two armies hold the ridges above the brook, Philistines on the one side and Israel on the other, and for forty days a giant out of Gath comes down between them and calls for a man. Jesse sends the boy up with parched corn and ten loaves for his brothers and ten cheeses for their captain. He refuses Saul's armour, chooses five smooth stones out of the brook, and goes down. One stone sinks in the giant's forehead. Elsewhere the same book gives the killing of Goliath the Gittite to Elhanan the son of Jaare-oregim.
stops.quote: Thou comest to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a shield: but I come to thee in the name of the Lord of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel, whom thou hast defied.
suggested_refs: The Elah brook between Socoh and Azekah, still full of smooth stones
2 Samuel 21:19, where Elhanan kills Goliath
sources: Wikipedia, 'David', on the duel as a hero-tale of Homeric type

segments.name: Saul's House, and the Flight From It

stops.name: Gibeah, the covenant with Jonathan
stops.date_confidence: traditional; the episode is undated in the text and follows the Goliath chapter immediately
stops.campa: The king's son hears David finish speaking to his father and the thing is settled in him at once. Jonathan strips himself of the robe that was upon him and gives it to David, and his garments, even to his sword and to his bow and to his girdle. Those are the marks an heir wears, handed over in front of the court. They make a covenant. The word the text uses for what is between them is love, without qualification. Nothing in the narrative suggests Saul understands what he has watched happen in his own hall.
stops.quote: And it came to pass, when he had made an end of speaking unto Saul, that the soul of Jonathan was knit with the soul of David, and Jonathan loved him as his own soul.
suggested_refs: 1 Samuel 18:1-4, the robe, the sword, the bow and the girdle

stops.name: Gibeah, the bride-price and the spear
stops.date_confidence: traditional; the marriage and the breach are undated, and the interval from the Goliath episode is a modern estimate
stops.campa: Saul offers his daughter Michal and names the price he expects will kill the suitor: a hundred foreskins of the Philistines. David brings two hundred and they are counted out in full tale before the king, though the Greek text and a later verse in Second Samuel both say a hundred, and the variant has never been resolved. The marriage is made. Then the women sing in the streets that Saul has slain his thousands and David his ten thousands, and the king takes up the javelin he keeps beside him and throws it twice at a man who is playing music for him. That night Michal lets her husband down through a window.
suggested_refs: 1 Samuel 18:25 against 18:27: the hundred demanded and the two hundred delivered
2 Samuel 3:14, where David later demands Michal back for a hundred

stops.name: Nob, the shewbread and the sword of Goliath
stops.date_confidence: traditional; the site of Nob is unidentified and the pin follows the customary placement near Mount Scopus
stops.campa: He arrives at the priests' town alone and hungry and lies about it, saying the king has sent him on business that requires haste. Ahimelech has no common bread and gives him the shewbread taken from before the Lord. Is there not here under thine hand spear or sword, David asks. There is one. The sword of the giant of Gath is kept there wrapped in a cloth behind the ephod, a trophy of the day that made his name, and he takes it and goes. Doeg the Edomite is standing in the precinct that day, detained before the Lord.
suggested_refs: 1 Samuel 22:9-19, where Doeg reports what he saw at Nob and kills eighty-five priests

stops.name: Gath, madness at the gate of Achish
stops.date_confidence: traditional; undated in the text, and the sequence rather than the year is what the narrative fixes
stops.campa: Of all the places a fugitive might run, he runs to the dead giant's own city, carrying the dead giant's sword. Achish's servants know the song about the ten thousands and repeat it in the hall. David is sore afraid, and changes his behaviour before them, and feigns himself mad in their hands, and scrabbles on the doors of the gate, and lets his spittle fall down upon his beard. They drive him out through the gate. Have I need of mad men, says Achish, that ye have brought this fellow to play the mad man in my presence?
suggested_refs: Tell es-Safi, widely identified with Philistine Gath

stops.name: The cave of Adullam, everyone in debt or in distress
stops.date_confidence: traditional; the coordinates follow the identification of Adullam with Khirbat esh-Sheikh Madkur, which no inscription has confirmed
stops.campa: He goes down to a cave in the broken limestone country between the Judaean hills and the Philistine plain, and his brothers and all his father's house go down to him there. Then others come, from no household at all: every one that was in distress, and every one that was in debt, and every one that was discontented, about four hundred men, and he becomes a captain over them. The same four hundred will be six hundred by the time he reaches Ziklag. His mother and father are in the cave with him, old.
suggested_refs: Khirbat esh-Sheikh Madkur, the leading candidate for Adullam
Khirbet 'Id el-Minya, the rival identification

stops.name: Mizpeh of Moab, the old man and woman put out of reach
stops.date_confidence: traditional; Mizpeh of Moab is unidentified and the pin approximates the Kerak plateau
stops.campa: He takes his father and mother across the Jordan and up onto the Moabite plateau and asks the king of Moab to let them stay until he knows what God will do for him. The chapter gives no reason at all for the choice of Moab. Later readers supply one, that his great-grandmother Ruth came out of this country and the family is claiming kin, but the text itself never mentions Ruth here. The parents remain in Moab while their son is in the hold. No later chapter returns to them.
suggested_refs: The Kerak plateau of Moab, where Mizpeh is conventionally sought
sources: Ruth 1-4, KJV, for the Moabite ancestry the passage does not invoke

stops.name: Horesh in the wilderness of Ziph, the last meeting with Jonathan
stops.date_confidence: traditional; this file's chronology lens placed the meeting before the Gath and Adullam episodes it actually follows, and the c. 1016 figure from the geography lens is used instead
stops.campa: In the wood at Horesh, in the dry hill country south of Hebron, the king's son comes out to find the outlaw and strengthens his hand in God. Thou shalt be king over Israel, Jonathan says, and I shall be next unto thee, and that also Saul my father knoweth. They make a covenant before the Lord, and Jonathan goes home to his father's house. They do not meet again. Twice the men of Ziph go up to Saul to tell him precisely where David is lying, and the wood at Horesh enters the record that way.
suggested_refs: 1 Samuel 23:16-18, the last covenant between David and Jonathan

stops.name: En Gedi, the corner of the robe
stops.date_confidence: traditional; the episode is undated and its place in the sequence is what the text fixes
stops.campa: Above the freshwater springs that break out of the cliff over the Dead Sea, in caves deep enough to hide three hundred men in the dark, Saul comes in alone to cover his feet. David's men tell him the day has been delivered into his hand. He goes forward and cuts off the skirt of Saul's robe privily, and afterwards his heart smites him even for that. He lets the king walk out, then calls down the slope with the cloth held up. Saul lifts up his voice and weeps and says, thou art more righteous than I, for thou hast rewarded me good, whereas I have rewarded thee evil.
stops.quote: The Lord forbid that I should do this thing unto my master, the Lord's anointed, to stretch forth mine hand against him, seeing he is the anointed of the Lord.
suggested_refs: The caves above the En Gedi springs on the western shore of the Dead Sea

stops.name: Carmel of Judah, Abigail on the pass with two hundred loaves
stops.date_confidence: traditional; undated in the text, placed here on narrative sequence
stops.campa: David's men have guarded Nabal's shearers all season and send to ask for provision at the feast, and Nabal answers that he does not know who David is. Four hundred men buckle on their swords. Abigail loads asses with two hundred loaves, two bottles of wine, five dressed sheep, five measures of parched corn, a hundred clusters of raisins and two hundred cakes of figs, and comes down by the covert of the hill without telling her husband. She meets the raid on the road and turns it with an argument. Ten days later Nabal is dead and she is David's wife.
suggested_refs: Carmel of Judah, near Maon, the estate of Nabal the Calebite

stops.name: Ziklag, the Philistine king's vassal
stops.date_confidence: traditional; the pin follows Garfinkel and Ganor's 2019 identification of Ziklag with Khirbet a-Ra'i, which Finkelstein and Maeir dispute, and at least fourteen sites have been proposed
stops.campa: He goes back to Gath, this time with six hundred men and their households behind him, and takes service under Achish, who gives him the border town of Ziklag for a seat. From there he raids the Geshurites and the Gezrites and the Amalekites and leaves no one alive to report which way he went, and tells Achish he has been raiding Judah. Achish believes him entirely and says, he hath made his people Israel utterly to abhor him, therefore he shall be my servant for ever. The arrangement lasts a year and four months.
suggested_refs: Khirbet a-Ra'i, west of Lachish, proposed as Ziklag in 2019
Tel Sera' / Tell esh-Shari'a, the older candidate some forty kilometres away

segments.name: Gilboa, and the Kingdom at Hebron

stops.name: Ziklag, the town burned and the spoil divided
stops.date_confidence: traditional; dated only by its place immediately before the Gilboa campaign in the narrative
stops.campa: The Philistine lords will not have him in their battle line against Israel and send him home. He comes back on the third day to find Ziklag burned with fire and the women and children carried off by an Amalekite raiding party, and the men who follow him talk of stoning him. He pursues with four hundred, two hundred being too faint to cross the brook Besor, and recovers every person taken. Then he rules that the share of the man who stayed by the stuff is the share of the man who went down to the battle, and makes it a statute in Israel.
suggested_refs: 1 Samuel 30:24-25, the statute on dividing spoil

stops.name: Mount Gilboa, Saul and Jonathan fall
stops.date_confidence: traditional; c. 1010 is reckoned back from the reign lengths of 2 Samuel 5:4-5 and is not independently attested
stops.campa: On the same days, sixty miles north, the Philistine army breaks Israel on the slopes of Gilboa. Jonathan is killed with his brothers. Saul, wounded by the archers, asks his armour-bearer to run him through and is refused, and falls on his own sword. David is not on the field, the Philistine lords having sent him home from their own battle line. The bodies are fastened to the wall of Beth-shan, and the men of Jabesh-gilead go by night and take them down and burn them and bury the bones under a tree.
suggested_refs: The ridge of Gilboa above the Jezreel valley
Jabesh-gilead, where Jonathan's bones were first buried

stops.name: Ziklag, the Song of the Bow
stops.date_confidence: traditional; the lament is undated and is placed by the narrative days after Gilboa
stops.campa: An Amalekite comes into the camp with his clothes rent and earth on his head, carrying Saul's crown and bracelet, and claims he finished the wounded king himself, expecting a reward. David has him killed for stretching out his hand against the anointed of the Lord. Then he makes the lament, and orders that the children of Judah be taught it, and it is written in the book of Jasher, a book that no longer exists anywhere. Tell it not in Gath, the lament says. Publish it not in the streets of Askelon.
stops.quote: The beauty of Israel is slain upon thy high places: how are the mighty fallen!
suggested_refs: The book of Jasher, cited in 2 Samuel 1:18 and Joshua 10:13, and lost

stops.name: Hebron, anointed king over Judah
stops.date_confidence: traditional; 2 Samuel 5:4-5 attaches the age of thirty to this accession and not to the later all-Israel anointing, and the year is a reckoning from those reign lengths
stops.campa: He asks whether he shall go up into any of the cities of Judah and is told to go to Hebron, the town of Abraham's burial, and he goes up with his two wives and his six hundred men and their households. The men of Judah come and anoint him king over the house of Judah. He is thirty years old. North of him Abner sets up Saul's surviving son Ish-bosheth at Mahanaim across the Jordan, and two kingdoms face one another over the same people. He reigns in Hebron seven years and six months. There is long war between the house of Saul and the house of David.
suggested_refs: 2 Samuel 5:4-5, on the thirty years and the seven years and six months at Hebron

stops.name: Hebron, the elders of all the tribes
stops.date_confidence: traditional; derived by adding the seven and a half Hebron years to the reckoned accession, with no external attestation
stops.campa: Abner falls out with Ish-bosheth over a concubine and opens negotiations to bring the north across, and Joab murders Abner in the gate of Hebron for his own brother's blood. Ish-bosheth is killed on his bed by two of his own captains, who carry the head to Hebron and are executed for it. Then all the tribes come to Hebron and say, behold, we are thy bone and thy flesh, and make a league with him before the Lord, and anoint him king over Israel. On the traditional reckoning he is about thirty-seven.
suggested_refs: The gate of Hebron, where Joab killed Abner

stops.name: Jerusalem, the stronghold of Zion and the tsinnor
stops.date_confidence: traditional; archaeologists dispute the scale of tenth-century Jerusalem, which excavation shows as a small and sparsely inhabited hill-country centre rather than a capital
stops.campa: The Jebusites hold a ridge between two valleys with a spring at its foot, and they tell him the blind and the lame will keep him out of it. He offers the command of the army to whoever goes up first by the tsinnor, a word of uncertain meaning that readers have taken for a water shaft, a gutter, a hook, a fortified passage. Joab goes up and is made chief. David takes the stronghold, calls it the city of David, and builds round about from the Millo inward. The ridge belongs to no tribe.
stops.quote: Nevertheless David took the strong hold of Zion: the same is the city of David.
suggested_refs: Warren's Shaft and the Middle Bronze fortified passage excavated by Reich and Shukron, rival candidates for the tsinnor
The City of David ridge above the Gihon spring
sources: Wikipedia, 'David', on the archaeology of tenth-century Jerusalem

stops.name: Kiriath-jearim, the Ark fetched off the hill
stops.date_confidence: traditional; 1 Samuel 7:2 gives twenty years at Kiriath-jearim, which does not reconcile with the intervening narrative
stops.campa: The chest that Moses had made in the wilderness has stood twenty years in the house of Abinadab on this hill, ever since the Philistines sent it back on a cart with the golden mice. David comes up with thirty thousand chosen men to carry it to the new capital. They set it on a new cart, which is how the Philistines had moved it and not how the law of Moses says it is moved, and Uzzah and Ahio drive the cart, and David and all the house of Israel play before it on harps and psalteries and timbrels and cornets and cymbals.
suggested_refs: The hill of Kiriath-jearim, called Baalah of Judah
Numbers 4 and 7:9, on carrying the ark upon the shoulders of the Kohathites

stops.name: Perez-uzzah, the hand put out to the Ark
stops.date_confidence: traditional; the site is unidentified and the pin approximates the ancient road between Kiriath-jearim and Jerusalem
stops.campa: At the threshingfloor of Nachon the oxen shake the cart and Uzzah puts out his hand to the ark of God and takes hold of it, and he dies there beside it. David is angry first and afraid afterwards, and asks how the ark of the Lord is to come to him at all. He will not take it another mile. He turns it aside into the house of Obed-edom the Gittite and leaves it there three months, and the procession to Jerusalem halts for a season. The place keeps the name Perez-uzzah, the breach upon Uzzah.
suggested_refs: The road from Kiriath-jearim down to Jerusalem, where Perez-uzzah is conventionally sought

stops.name: Jerusalem, the king dancing in a linen ephod
stops.date_confidence: traditional; three months after the halt at Obed-edom's house, per 2 Samuel 6:11, with no absolute date in the text
stops.campa: Word comes that the Lord has blessed the house of Obed-edom because of the ark, and David goes and fetches it up with gladness. He dances before the Lord with all his might, whirling, girded in a plain linen ephod that Rashi glosses as a priest's garment worn by a king, not the robes of state. Michal, Saul's daughter, watches from a window and despises him in her heart; when he comes home she calls him one of the riff-raff, shamelessly uncovered before the handmaids. He answers that before the Lord he will make himself lighter still, and by those same handmaids be held in honor. She has no child unto the day of her death.
stops.quote_source: Rashi on 2 Samuel 6:20, trans. via Sefaria, glossing Michal's word achad ha-reikim by Targum Yonatan's Aramaic
suggested_refs: The tent David pitched for the ark on the City of David ridge
Rashi on 2 Samuel 6:14 and 6:22, on the ephod and David's retort

stops.name: Jerusalem, Nathan and the promise of a house
stops.date_confidence: traditional; this file's two research lenses dated 2 Samuel 7 and 2 Samuel 9 in an order that reverses the chapters, and the narrative order is kept here instead
stops.campa: The king, settled in a house of cedar, tells Nathan it is not fitting that the ark of God should dwell within curtains. Nathan says, go, do all that is in thine heart. That night the word comes back the other way: the Lord will build him a house instead, meaning a line and not a building, and his seed after him shall build for the name, and the throne shall be established for ever. The gospels will open by tracing Jesus to this promise through Bethlehem, and Haile Selassie will be crowned in Addis Ababa as the two hundred and twenty-fifth monarch of the line it opens.
suggested_refs: 2 Samuel 7:12-16, the dynastic covenant
The Kebra Nagast, which carries the line to Aksum through Menelik

stops.name: Jerusalem, Mephibosheth at the king's table
stops.date_confidence: traditional; undated in the text and placed after 2 Samuel 7 on narrative order, against one of this file's research lenses which put it earlier
stops.campa: He asks whether any is left of the house of Saul, that he may show the kindness of God to him for Jonathan's sake, and Ziba names a son of Jonathan lame on both his feet, dropped by his nurse in the panic after Gilboa when he was five years old. Mephibosheth is brought from Lo-debar and falls on his face. David restores to him all the land of Saul his grandfather, sets Ziba and his fifteen sons and twenty servants to till it, and seats him at the royal table as one of the king's own sons. He eats there continually, and he is lame on both his feet.
suggested_refs: 2 Samuel 4:4, on the nurse who dropped the child in the flight from Gilboa

stops.name: Jerusalem, the roof and the woman washing
stops.date_confidence: traditional; dated only by the Ammonite campaign it interrupts, which the text itself does not date
stops.campa: At the time when kings go forth to battle the king does not go. Joab besieges Rabbah and David stays in Jerusalem. He rises at eventide and walks upon the roof, and from the roof he sees a woman washing herself, very beautiful to look upon. He sends and enquires after her. They tell him she is Bathsheba the daughter of Eliam, wife of Uriah the Hittite, one of his own thirty champions. The same verse notes she is purifying herself from her uncleanliness, which Rashi reads as confirming no child could yet be Uriah's own. He sends messengers and takes her. Afterwards she sends word that she is with child.
stops.quote: From her uncleanliness: from her menstrual impurity.
suggested_refs: 2 Samuel 23:39, where Uriah the Hittite is named last in the roll of the mighty men

stops.name: Rabbah of the Ammonites, Uriah set in the forefront
stops.date_confidence: traditional; the siege of Rabbah is undated in the text and the year follows the preceding stop
stops.campa: Uriah is recalled from the siege and will not go down to his own house while the ark and Israel and Judah abide in tents, and sleeps at the palace door among the servants, sober and then drunk, twice refusing the cover the king needs from him. So David writes to Joab and sends the letter by Uriah's own hand: set ye Uriah in the forefront of the hottest battle, and retire ye from him, that he may be smitten, and die. Joab does it at the wall. Word comes back that certain of the servants are dead, and thy servant Uriah the Hittite is dead also.
suggested_refs: Rabbath-Ammon, beneath the citadel of modern Amman

stops.name: Jerusalem, the parable of the ewe lamb
stops.date_confidence: traditional; undated in the text, placed by narrative sequence within a year of the death of Uriah
stops.campa: Nathan comes to the palace with a case for judgment: a rich man with many flocks took the poor man's one ewe lamb, which lay in his bosom and was unto him as a daughter, to feed a traveller. The king's anger is kindled and he says the man shall surely die. Thou art the man, Nathan says: I gave thee thy master's house and thy master's wives, wives Rashi names as Michal, who once despised him for dancing before the ark. The sword shall never depart from thine house, he reads, and evil shall rise against thee out of thine own house. The child sickens. David fasts seven days on the ground, and when it dies he gets up and washes and eats.
stops.quote: And David said unto Nathan, I have sinned against the Lord. And Nathan said unto David, The Lord also hath put away thy sin; thou shalt not die.
suggested_refs: Psalm 51, attached to this episode by its superscription, which modern scholarship reads as a late editorial heading
Rashi on 2 Samuel 12:8, identifying 'thy master's wives' as Michal
sources: Wikipedia, 'Book of Psalms', on the superscriptions

stops.name: Jerusalem, Solomon born in the house of David
stops.date_confidence: traditional; the birth is undated in the text and the figure is a convention, given elsewhere as c. 990 BC
stops.campa: Bathsheba bears another son in the house on the ridge and David calls him Shelomoh, Solomon. Nathan comes with a second name sent from the Lord, Jedidiah, beloved of the Lord, which the record sets down once and then never uses again. The household he is born into still has the murdered husband in it and the sentence Nathan read out over it. He will be handed the kingdom over the heads of older brothers. The temple goes up on the threshingfloor his father buys and is not permitted to build on.
suggested_refs: 2 Samuel 12:24-25, the two names given to the child

segments.name: The Sword in His Own House

stops.name: Baal-hazor, the sheepshearing and Amnon's blood
stops.date_confidence: traditional; this file's two research lenses dated this killing thirteen years apart, at c. 993 and c. 980, and c. 990 is chosen so that the text's own intervals of three, two and four years land the revolt near 979
stops.campa: Amnon, the eldest son, feigns sickness and rapes his half-sister Tamar in his own chamber, and then hates her with a hatred greater than the love wherewith he had loved her, and puts her out and bolts the door after her. David hears of it and is very wroth and does nothing at all. Two years later Absalom holds a sheepshearing at Baal-hazor and asks for all the king's sons, and when Amnon's heart is merry with wine his servants kill him at the table. The other princes rise and flee on their mules. Absalom rides for Geshur.
suggested_refs: Baal-hazor near Ephraim, the highest summit of the central hill country

stops.name: Geshur, three years with his mother's father
stops.date_confidence: traditional; the three years are 2 Samuel 13:38, and the coordinates follow the identification of Geshur with et-Tell / Bethsaida, which is contested
stops.campa: Absalom's mother is Maacah, daughter of Talmai king of Geshur, and it is to his grandfather's small Aramean kingdom east of the sea of Galilee that he goes, and there he stays three years. David mourns for Amnon and is comforted, and the soul of the king longs to go forth unto Absalom. Joab reads him, and hires a wise woman of Tekoah to bring the king a false case about two sons and a blood feud, and argues him into fetching a murderer home. The order is given. Absalom crosses back over the Jordan.
suggested_refs: Et-Tell, near Bethsaida, the leading candidate for the capital of Geshur
2 Samuel 3:3, where Maacah daughter of Talmai is named as Absalom's mother

stops.name: Jerusalem, two years without the king's face, then the gate
stops.date_confidence: traditional; 2 Samuel 14:28 gives two full years and 15:7 gives four more, following the Septuagint and Syriac, since the Masoretic reading of forty is impossible
stops.campa: Let him turn to his own house, David says, and let him not see my face. Absalom dwells two full years in Jerusalem and does not see the king. He sends twice for Joab, who will not come, and burns Joab's barley field to make him come, and is finally brought in and kissed. Then he gets himself chariots and horses and fifty men to run before him, and rises early to stand beside the way of the gate, and tells every man with a suit that his cause is good but there is no man deputed of the king to hear him. So he steals the hearts of the men of Israel.
suggested_refs: 2 Samuel 14:28-33, the burnt barley field
2 Samuel 15:7, where the Masoretic forty years is corrected to four in the Greek and Syriac

stops.name: The Mount of Olives, the king goes up barefoot
stops.date_confidence: traditional; c. 979 is the figure both research lenses of this file agree on for the flight, reached by different arithmetic
stops.campa: The message comes that the hearts of the men of Israel are after Absalom, who has had himself proclaimed king at Hebron, the town where his father was anointed twice. David leaves the city on foot with his household and his guard and six hundred Gittites, and sends the ark back into Jerusalem, saying that if he finds favour he will see it again and if not, let the Lord do as seems good. He goes up the ascent of Olivet weeping, his head covered and his feet bare, and all the people with him cover their heads and go up weeping as they go.
stops.quote: And David went up by the ascent of mount Olivet, and wept as he went up, and had his head covered, and he went barefoot.
suggested_refs: The ascent of the Mount of Olives east of the Kidron

stops.name: Mahanaim, beds and honey brought out to a fugitive king
stops.date_confidence: traditional; Mahanaim is identified with Tell edh-Dhahab el-Gharbi on the Jabbok, an identification the excavators themselves describe as uncertain
stops.campa: He crosses the Jordan by night and comes to Mahanaim in Gilead, the town where Ish-bosheth once kept a rival throne against him. Shobi the Ammonite, Machir of Lo-debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite bring out beds and basons and earthen vessels, wheat and barley and flour and parched corn, beans and lentils, honey and butter and sheep and cheese of kine, for the people are hungry and weary and thirsty in the wilderness. The men who have come with him are counted in the gate and set under three captains.
suggested_refs: Tulul adh-Dhahab on the Zarqa, the twin tells assigned to Mahanaim and Penuel

stops.name: The Forest of Ephraim, the oak and the three darts
stops.date_confidence: traditional; the site is unidentified beyond east of the Jordan and the pin is an approximation
stops.campa: He wants to march out with them and they will not have it, saying he is worth ten thousand of them. So he stands in the gate as the army files past and says in the hearing of all the captains, deal gently for my sake with the young man, even with Absalom. The battle spreads over the face of the whole country, and the wood devours more people that day than the sword devours. Absalom's mule goes under a great oak and his head catches in the boughs and he hangs there living. Joab takes three darts in his hand and thrusts them through his heart.
suggested_refs: 2 Samuel 18:5, the order given in the gate and overheard by the whole army

stops.name: Mahanaim, the chamber over the gate
stops.date_confidence: traditional; the same day or the day after the battle, per 2 Samuel 18:24-33
stops.campa: The watchman on the roof sees a man running, and then another, and Ahimaaz arrives crying that all is well and will not say the thing he knows. Then Cushi comes and says, the enemies of my lord the king, and all that rise against thee to do thee hurt, be as that young man is. The king goes up to the chamber over the gate. Joab comes in afterwards and tells him plainly that he has shamed the men who saved his life and his wives and his children, and that unless he goes down and speaks kindly to them by nightfall not one of them will stay.
stops.quote: O my son Absalom, my son, my son Absalom! would God I had died for thee, O Absalom, my son, my son!
suggested_refs: 2 Samuel 19:1-8, Joab's rebuke in the chamber over the gate

stops.name: Jerusalem, the king brought back over Jordan
stops.date_confidence: traditional; the return follows the battle by weeks in the narrative and has no date of its own
stops.campa: The tribes fall to arguing over who has the right to fetch him, and the men of Judah come down to Gilgal to bring him over the Jordan, and the quarrel between Israel and Judah is not settled at the ford. Shimei, who cursed him and threw stones at him on the road out, meets him there with a thousand Benjamites and is pardoned. Barzillai, eighty years old, comes down to the river and refuses to go up to Jerusalem, saying he can no longer taste what he eats or drinks or hear singing men and singing women, and asks only to die in his own city by the graves of his father and mother.
suggested_refs: 2 Samuel 19:40-43, the dispute between the men of Israel and the men of Judah at the ford

segments.name: The Threshing Floor and the Charge

stops.name: Jerusalem, the threshingfloor of Araunah the Jebusite
stops.date_confidence: traditional; this file's research pool dated the purchase two years after David's own death, and the c. 975 figure from the geography lens is used instead
stops.campa: He numbers the people over Joab's protest, and the counting itself is counted a sin, and a pestilence falls. The angel stops at the threshingfloor of Araunah the Jebusite, and David is sent up to build an altar there. Araunah offers the ground and the oxen and the threshing instruments for wood as a gift. Nay, but I will surely buy it of thee at a price, David says, neither will I offer burnt offerings unto the Lord my God of that which doth cost me nothing. Second Samuel says fifty shekels of silver. First Chronicles says six hundred shekels of gold.
suggested_refs: The rock beneath the Dome of the Rock, traditionally the threshingfloor
2 Chronicles 3:1, the only text that calls the site Moriah

stops.name: Shunem, the girl brought to warm the failing king
stops.date_confidence: traditional; dated only by its position at the opening of 1 Kings, months before the death
stops.campa: He is old and stricken in years, and they cover him with clothes and he gets no heat. His servants propose a remedy: let there be sought for my lord the king a young virgin, and let her stand before the king and cherish him, and let her lie in thy bosom, that my lord the king may get heat. They search all the coasts of Israel and find Abishag the Shunammite, fair to look on, and bring her to Jerusalem, and she ministers to him. Adonijah has already begun saying that he will be king. The king knew her not, the text says.
suggested_refs: 1 Kings 2:13-25, where Adonijah asks for Abishag and is executed for asking

stops.name: The Gihon spring, Solomon anointed while David lives
stops.date_confidence: traditional; the anointing is undated in the text and falls in David's last year on the conventional reckoning
stops.campa: Adonijah, the eldest surviving son, has already killed sheep and oxen and fat cattle at En-rogel with Joab and Abiathar and all the king's other sons, and has invited neither Nathan nor Benaiah nor Solomon. Nathan sends Bathsheba into the bedchamber to remind the dying king of an oath. David gives the order from the bed: set Solomon on the king's own mule, take him down to Gihon, let Zadok and Nathan anoint him there, blow the trumpet and say, God save king Solomon. The city rings until the ground cleaves with the sound, and Adonijah's guests hear it from the spring below and scatter.
suggested_refs: The Gihon spring in the Kidron, and En-rogel downstream where Adonijah feasted

stops.name: Jerusalem, the charge to Solomon and the death
stops.date_confidence: traditional; c. 970 is reckoned from the forty-year reign of 1 Kings 2:11 and has no external attestation
stops.campa: He calls his son in and speaks like a man handing over a going concern. Be strong, and show thyself a man, and keep the charge of the Lord thy God, walking in his ways and keeping his statutes as it is written in the law of Moses, which is the law carried out of the wilderness in the ark he brought up the ridge. Then come the practical clauses, about Joab and Shimei and the debts still open. So David slept with his fathers, and was buried in the city of David. The days that he reigned over Israel were forty years.
stops.quote: I go the way of all the earth: be thou strong therefore, and shew thyself a man; and keep the charge of the Lord thy God, to walk in his ways, to keep his statutes, and his commandments, and his judgments, and his testimonies, as it is written in the law of Moses.
suggested_refs: 1 Kings 2:10-12, the burial in the city of David and the forty years

stops.name: The City of David, the grave that has not been found
stops.date_confidence: traditional for the burial; the archaeological work described here is dated 2005 and 2014 and is placed at this pin because it concerns the same ridge
stops.campa: He is buried inside the walls of his own city, on the ridge above the Gihon, against the ordinary practice of burying outside a settlement, and the sepulchres of the kings are still spoken of as a known place centuries later. Nothing certainly his has ever been dug. In 2005 Eilat Mazar excavated a Large Stone Structure on this ridge and proposed it as his palace, citing Phoenician ivory inlays and red-slipped hand-burnished bowls. Israel Finkelstein reads much of it as Hasmonean, and a radiocarbon sample from the fill returned a range of 1050 to 780 BC.
suggested_refs: The Large Stone Structure on the City of David ridge, excavated from February 2005
Doron Ben-Ami's 2014 season, which found no tenth-century city wall in the western area

stops.name: Tel Dan, bytdwd cut in basalt
stops.date_confidence: inferred; the stele is dated to the ninth century BC on palaeographic and stratigraphic grounds, and 830 is a midpoint within that range, not a recorded year
stops.campa: Far to the north, at the mound above the springs of the Jordan, an Aramean king sets up a victory stele in the gate and boasts on it of kings he has killed. The stone is later broken up and built into a wall. In July 1993 a fragment comes out of that wall carrying the letters bytdwd, house of david, and two more fragments follow in June 1994. It is the earliest accepted mention of the dynasty outside the Hebrew Bible, written by an enemy, roughly a century and a half after the man it names as founder. A minority read the letters as something else.
suggested_refs: The Tel Dan Stele fragments in the Israel Museum, Jerusalem
Biran and Naveh's excavation reports of 1993 and 1995

stops.name: Mount Zion, the cenotaph on the wrong hill
stops.date_confidence: traditional; the tradition of a tomb on this hill first appears in the ninth century of the common era and no year is recorded, so the date is a placeholder within that century
stops.campa: The tradition that puts his tomb on this hill begins in the ninth century of the common era, on a rise the biblical writers did not call Zion, and the Crusaders build the Gothic cenotaph that stands there now. The room has been a church, then a mosque after the Franciscans were expelled in 1523 and the Cenacle above was converted in 1524, and since 1948 a synagogue, with the room of the Last Supper still on the floor overhead. Historians, archaeologists and the rabbinate all hold that the king is not under it, and pilgrims have gone up to it for eleven hundred years.
suggested_refs: The Crusader cenotaph and the parochet laid over it after 1948
The 1524 inscription on the east wall of the Cenacle

stops.name: Florence, the marble shepherd before the palace
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Michelangelo takes a block of Carrara marble another sculptor had botched and abandoned and cuts from it a naked youth over four metres tall, sling slung over the shoulder, stone in the right hand, the head turned toward something outside the block. He works from September 1501 into 1504. On the eighth of September 1504 it is set up outside the Palazzo della Signoria, facing Rome, and a republic that expects to be attacked adopts the giant-killer as its own portrait. The marble goes indoors to the Accademia in 1873, and a copy has stood in the square since 1910.
suggested_refs: The David in the Galleria dell'Accademia, Florence
Donatello's bronze David, the first freestanding nude male bronze since antiquity
